A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FSA work. The complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite the new layout, appendix renumbering, and added material.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original GPU latency benchmarks and optimization ablations. Appendix C reports Llama3-8B fine-tuning loss on ML-ArXiv-Papers.

after.justification: The original empirical results are retained, with additional QA accuracy measurements, memory and compilation profiling, long-context benchmarks, and distributed inference experiments in Appendices D–I.

M1.justification: The inverted KV/query loops, index mappings, early termination, and separate softmax and reduction kernels are retained. Attention-sink buffering and cached profiling with NSA fallback already appear in v2 Appendix D and remain in v3 Appendix E; the new evaluations do not document a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 retains ML-ArXiv-Papers and adds LongBench HotpotQA multi-document QA, Qasper single-document QA, and PassR-EN synthetic QA in Appendix D. Appendix F also extends evaluated inputs to 128K and 256K contexts, substantially broadening task and input coverage.

E2.justification: NSA and Triton-based Flash Attention remain the main comparators. v3 adds an evaluated FlashDecoding baseline alongside NSA and FSA in the decoding comparison in Table 10; v2 contains no FlashDecoding evaluation.

E3.justification: New accuracy experiments introduce Llama-3.2-1B/3B and Llama-3.1-8B, 2K-step loss measurements for the smaller models, and perplexity and QA F1 metrics. Additional protocols specify 512-token generation, decoding averaged over 1K generated tokens, and tensor-parallel degrees 1/2/4/8. These expand the evaluation design without documenting revisions to the retained benchmarks.

E4.justification: The original optimization ablations and timing breakdowns remain. v3 adds empirical buffer-scaling measurements (Table 5), compilation-cost profiling (Table 11), and tensor-parallel scaling studies (Tables 12–15), substantially extending analysis of memory, startup, and distributed execution costs.

E5.justification: Both versions report point results and aggregate averages without independent run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. Averaging over generated tokens or training steps in v3 does not introduce repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing plotted results and headline speedups are retained, while Tables 2–15 add accuracy, memory, compilation, long-context, and distributed results. For example, Table 10 reports 256K H20 decoding latencies of 0.61 ms for FSA, 0.62 ms for NSA, and 5.76 ms for FlashDecoding. These are additional measurements, not improvements to previously reported v2 scores.

T1.justification: The attention equations, Section 3.3 theorem, and memory/FLOPs derivations and assumptions are retained. v2 Appendix D becomes v3 Appendix E; the added buffer measurements do not revise its mathematical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same kernel contribution and applicability to small GQA groups. Maximum speedup claims remain 3.5× for kernels, 1.25× for training, and 1.36× for prefill; new experiments provide supporting evidence.

C2.justification: Appendix G adds an explanation linking FlashDecoding's KV partitioning to parallelism and FSA's advantage to sparsity. Appendix D interprets the new QA results as matching NSA and full attention, although the full-attention equivalence is broader than Tables 3–4 support. Existing buffering and memory-access tradeoffs remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies BF16 training and FP16 inference and supplies head counts, head dimensions, and generation budgets for added benchmarks. The implementation appendix, warp allocations, buffer/fallback details, and repository link are retained. The precision statement is newly disclosed information, not evidence that existing experiments changed precision.

R1.justification: v3 adds nine references, including Flash-Decoding, LongBench, CHAI, and InfLLM. The main related-work discussion and positioning as an alternative NSA implementation remain essentially unchanged; the author-year citation conversion is formatting.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose are retained with localized grammatical editing. v3 adds author contact details, acknowledgments, an LLM writing-use disclosure, appendix headings, and cross-references, while renumbering the existing appendices.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the branded title and boxed abstract with the ICLR template and changes typography and page composition. Figures 2–3 are reduced and wrapped beside text, Figures 7–10 are grouped on one page, and Tables 2–15 add extensive tabular displays. Existing figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens practical validation through task-level FSA–NSA accuracy checks, measured buffer and compilation costs, and longer-context and distributed evaluations. These provide useful evidence beyond v2's training-loss curve and analytical buffer estimate. The gain is tempered by unspecified splits and uncertainty in the new QA evaluation, and an overstated full-attention equivalence: Table 3 reports 3B Qasper perplexity of 2.64 for FSA versus 1.20 for full attention.
